title: Immaculate Constellation USAP managed by DoD but held at the White House

tellings.quote: I will say that after I published I was told that this program that the usap was actually um managed by the Department of Defense but held at the White House
it's actually ran out of and owned by the National Security Council out of the White House.
tellings.difference: Brown says the NSC runs and owns it, not that DoD manages it, and calls it an old mission that predates 2017.
tellings.link_reason: Both say Immaculate Constellation is held at the White House. Shellenberger's story says it is held there; Brown says it is run and owned by the NSC there.

as_told.title: Immaculate Constellation actually an old NSC-owned mission

plain: The story is about Immaculate Constellation, said to be an unacknowledged special access program, meaning a secret US government program whose existence is not officially admitted, which supposedly gathers UFO data. The journalist Michael Shellenberger, who published a report on the program in 2024, says that after it came out he was told the program was "managed by the Department of Defense but held at the White House." In other words, the Pentagon ran it day to day, but it sat under the President's own house. A Pentagon whistleblower named Matthew Brown tells it differently, passing on what he was told. He says the program is "ran out of and owned by the National Security Council," the President's own security staff at the White House, rather than managed by the Pentagon. Brown also calls it an old mission that started well before 2017. Both accounts come from unnamed sources speaking to the tellers, and if either is right, it would mean the secret UFO effort reaches all the way to the White House.
